dedupe_keys.name: europe s transport infrastructure is not ready to face climate change multi hazard exposure of roads rail waterways and airports

description: This NHESS article (published 22 July 2026) reviews observed impacts of climate extremes on Europe's transport network and presents a multi-hazard analysis, designed to be accessible to policymakers, of the exposure of four transport modes to river floods, heatwaves, droughts and wildfires. The review uses the GDIS geocoded version of EM-DAT, the DRMKC Risk Data Hub for road and rail flood losses (2010 to 2022), a EUROCONTROL aviation climate risk report and the JRC European Drought Risk Atlas, plus four case studies: the 2018 heatwave and drought in Germany, the 2021 floods in Belgium, Germany and the Netherlands, the 2021 to 2023 flash floods in Greece and a compound event. Extremes already affect all modes, with the 2018 Rhine drought alone costing EUR 2.4 billion, and exposure could rise substantially by mid-century, relevant to TEN-T investment. Coverage: EU transport networks. Format and access: open access article. Licence and cost: CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: exposure, not damage modelling. It supports hazard exposure and climate adaptation studies. It relates to EM-DAT, TEN-T maps, the Rhine 2018 low-water case and the global rail and road exposure study in the catalogue.
